thesis: An acquirer is only as good as the industries it buys into. For each serial acquirer: which industries it owns and buys, where those industries are heading according to published forecasts and data, and whether its new deals point toward stronger or weaker industries than the business it already has.

layers.title: 1 · Industry map
layers.question: Which industries does each company own and buy?

steps.label: Disclosed deals
steps.detail: Acquisitions with SEDAR quotes, copied from engine/input/deals.json.

steps.label: Deal industry labels
steps.detail: A NAICS code per deal, with the quote that justifies it, approved by a person (engine/input/outlook-labels.csv).

steps.label: Revenue by segment
steps.detail: Onesheet segments for CSU, TOI, WSP, TFII, ARE, each segment mapped to NAICS.

layers.title: 2 · Industry signals
layers.question: Where is each industry heading, according to published sources?

steps.label: Recent momentum
steps.detail: Statistics Canada GDP by industry (table 36-10-0434), 3-year yearly rate.

steps.label: Official projection
steps.detail: US BLS Employment Projections and Canada COPS outlook by industry.

steps.label: Street forecast
steps.detail: Median analyst revenue growth estimate of the public companies in that industry (Onesheet estimates).

steps.label: Narrative
steps.detail: News and earnings-call quotes summarized by Claude. Shown as text, never scored.

layers.title: 3 · Company tailwind
layers.question: How strong are the industries this company earns its money in?

steps.label: Industry outlook
steps.detail: One declared blend of the signals (start: median of the available ones), in engine/metrics.ts with tests.

steps.label: Revenue-weighted tailwind
steps.detail: Share of revenue × industry outlook, with the share of revenue covered shown.

layers.title: 4 · Direction
layers.question: Are the new deals heading toward stronger or weaker industries than the existing business?

steps.label: Deals vs base
steps.detail: Outlook of the last 3 years' deals vs the existing revenue mix: toward ↗, steady →, or away ↘.
